scope: Bind imported DXF POINTCLOUDEX callbacks in ENTITIES and named BLOCKS to exact physical records and the retained output entity; keep imported graph output refused.

behavior: DXF ENTITIES delivery events are joined through their dispatch span to the exact complete POINTCLOUDEX physical record and parser-produced typed model snapshot.

Named BLOCK POINTCLOUDEX callbacks retain an additional bounded typed snapshot keyed by the actual dispatch; the block callback, physical child record and current output entity must agree on identity, owner and the complete modeled entity state.
Physical spans, source revision/encoding, generation/container ownership, one-to-one record/callback/output counts and duplicate source/output identities are checked before graph preparation.
The extra POINTCLOUDEX BLOCK snapshots include nested point/cropping payload sizes in their retained-byte and work budget accounting.

Imported DXF output remains refused after source binding until full physical-field-to-writer projection and source-derived DefinitionEx/ReactorEx graph output are qualified. An authored standalone zero-reference POINTCLOUDEX transport route remains permitted.

validationProfile.source: Locally generated point-cloud graph written to temporary files by the adapter test; no repository or external DWG/DXF fixtures were added.
assertions: Imported generated POINTCLOUDEX has a complete source-binding report with exactly one bound entity in each encoding.
The source-bound imported graph is still refused for output and the pre-existing destination sentinel remains byte-identical.
The authored graph, reference-refusal, destination-preservation, corrected-retry and typed-readback controls continue to pass.

limitations: This joins a parser callback/model to a physical record; it does not independently adjudicate POINTCLOUDEX field meanings or prove that all accepted physical fields survive serialization.

Imported DXF graph output, DWG source CLASS/frame/output binding, recursive graph closure, physical producer breadth, external asset loading, native 3D consumer behavior and platform qualification remain open.
